title: Japan home loans: start with the rate structure
summary: An initial reading map for Japan: what stays fixed, what can reset, and which conditions deserve a closer look.

takeaways.text: Distinguish variable, initial fixed-period and full-term fixed borrowing.
Read the repayment rules alongside the rate.

sections.heading: Three structures, different exposure
sections.text: MUFG describes variable rates, a selected fixed period followed by a new choice, and full-term fixed borrowing. These structures carry different exposure to later rate changes.

sections.heading: A payment rule is not a rate cap
sections.text: At MUFG, variable-rate equal-payment loans use five-year payment reviews and a 125% limit on the revised payment. Equal-principal loans do not. Interest can still rise; unpaid interest may be deferred. These are product-specific rules, not a promise about every Japanese loan.

sections.heading: Our starting point
sections.text: This is a baseline explainer, not a forecast or a report of a new policy decision. Compare reset mechanics, total fees and borrower conditions before comparing headline percentages.
